title: Felix and the Ember
premise: Mirabel Okafor was exiled to the Ember Valley as a child because storm-calling magic dies at its borders, and for twenty years he has lived content in the one place the crown's watchers cannot see him. When the valley's ancient wards collapse on the same night every star vanishes from the sky, he learns the truth: the wards were his mother's dying spell, and their fall means the thing wearing King Aldous's crown—the Hollow Regent, a memory-eating parasite—has finally found the last bloodline it cannot digest. Guided by the ember of his mother's magic and a disgraced royal archivist named Sef, Mirabel must cross a starless kingdom where stolen memories walk as ghosts, gathering the scattered recollections of the true king before the thirteenth moon turns and the Regent consumes Aldous entirely. At the climax, Mirabel chooses to give up his own most precious memory to rekindle the king's, unbinding Aldous and shattering the Regent—but in doing so he forgets the valley, his mother, and the reason he ever fought, and the final chapters follow his slow, aching relearning of a life that now belongs to someone he used to be.
about_author: Juniper Nystrom is a former archivist from the northern fjord country who writes fantasies about what institutions choose to remember and what they bury. She lives in a converted lighthouse with two opinionated gulls and a growing collection of untranslatable words.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Mirabel Okafor's POV. He repairs a neighbor's roof and quietly douses a lightning storm with his bare hands, a magic that only works inside the valley. Establishes his exile, his routine, and his deliberate smallness. Beat: comfort shadowed by the knowledge that he has never once seen the stars leave the sky.

chapters.title: Ward-Stones
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The valley's border stones hum on the equinox; old Wrenna tells him they were set by a woman who 'paid with her whole self.' Mirabel touches one and hears a fragment of his mother's voice. Beat: first crack in his belief that the valley is simply home rather than a prison.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Every star vanishes at once; the ward-stones shatter like dropped porcelain. Storm-magic floods back into him, violent and unpracticed. He watches a rider in royal livery fall dead at the border, clutching a sealed letter. Beat: terror and exhilaration entangled.

chapters.title: The Letter in Dead Hands
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The letter names him: 'the Okafor heir is located; the Regent's patience is ended.' He realizes his invisibility was engineered, and now it's over. Beat: grief for the safe life he didn't know was a cage.

chapters.title: What the Valley Kept
chapters.summary: Wrenna's POV. She reveals she was his mother's friend and keeper of her secrets: the wards were Mirabel's mother's final spell, bought with her memories. Beat: betrayal and tenderness—Wrenna lied for twenty years to give him a childhood.

chapters.title: The Ember
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Wrenna gives him an ember-glass pendant holding his mother's last preserved memory. When he holds it, he feels her storm-calling and a single image: a king, weeping, asking her to hide her son. Beat: inheritance reframed—not property, but obligation.

chapters.title: Leaving
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He crosses the border for the first time. The world beyond is starless, gray, and full of people who don't remember last winter. Beat: vertigo of freedom that feels like falling.

chapters.title: The Road of Unremembered Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He passes villages where the Hollow Regent's tithe-collectors have taken memories as tax. A woman offers him bread in exchange for the memory of her own daughter's face, which she can no longer hold. Beat: the cost of the kingdom's 'peace' made flesh.

chapters.title: The Archivist in the Well
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Sef's POV. He rescues Sef Vane, a royal archivist thrown down a well for cataloguing the Regent's thefts. Sharp, bitter, indispensable—Sef knows where the king's stolen memories were hidden. Beat: wary alliance; Mirabel's first ally outside the valley.

chapters.title: The Hollow Regent
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Exposition through Sef's forbidden chronicle: the Regent is a parasite that entered the palace forty years ago, eating the king's memories one by one and ruling through his hollowed face. Beat: dread; the enemy is patient and institutional, not a monster in a lair.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Sef explains the deadline: when the moon completes its thirteenth turn, the last of King Aldous will dissolve and the Regent becomes permanent. They must find the king's hidden memories before then. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Salt Cathedral
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. First memory-vault: a drowned cathedral where the Regent's early thefts were smuggled out by loyalists. Mirabel's storm-magic parts the flood. Beat: competence and awe—his exile-gift is a weapon here.

chapters.title: A Memory of Rain
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Inside the vault he touches a vial of the king's memory: Aldous as a young man, dancing in a storm, alive in a way the hollow king never is. Beat: Mirabel falls a little in love with a man he's never met.

chapters.title: The Tithe-Collector
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Sef's POV. A Regent collector corners them; Sef offers a false memory to buy escape, and Mirabel sees how easily memory can be forged—and how much of himself he's trusting to Sef. Beat: first real danger; trust tested and holding.

chapters.title: Ghosts of the Borrowed
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Stolen memories, discarded by the Regent, walk the moors as mindless ghosts. One ghost wears Mirabel's mother's face—only a fragment, repeating a lullaby. Beat: heartbreak; the dead are not at rest while their memories are currency.

chapters.title: The Loyalist Cell
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. They find the remnant loyalists hiding in a chalk mine, led by a former palace guard, Odile. They've protected three memory-vaults for decades but are down to nine people. Beat: hope with a body count; the resistance is dying of old age.

chapters.title: What Odile Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her testimony: the king asked for his memories to be scattered because he felt the Regent feeding and wanted nothing left worth eating. Beat: the king as co-author of his own erasure—complicating the rescue.

chapters.title: Vault of the First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The second vault holds the king's memory of the Regent's arrival—including who invited it in. Beat: the past is not innocent; the court itself opened the door.

chapters.title: The Name in the Vial
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The betrayer's name is in the vial: Sef's own mentor, the former Royal Archivist. Sef's life's work was built on a lie. Beat: Sef's crisis; the alliance wobbles under shame.

chapters.title: Interlude at the Crossroads Inn
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A quiet chapter: the group rests, Mirabel teaches a child in the inn to whistle thunder, and he and Sef argue about whether the king deserves saving at all. Beat: breath before the plunge; the theme argued openly.

chapters.title: The Regent's Eye
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Regent, aware of the thefts, sends its gaze—a starless patch of moving darkness. It finds them at the third vault's threshold. Beat: the enemy becomes personal and present.

chapters.title: The Third Vault, Broken
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Regent reaches the vault first and drinks the memories in front of them. Mirabel's storm-magic barely drives it off; Odile dies holding the empty vials. Beat: devastating loss; the plan is now half-ruined.

chapters.title: Ash and Accusation
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The surviving loyalists blame Sef's mentor's trail for the ambush. Mirabel defends him, and the group fractures and reforms around a harsher plan: go to the palace itself. Beat: resolve forged in grief.

chapters.title: The Starless City
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They enter the capital, where the Regent's hunger is visible—citizens bright-eyed and vacant, streets scrubbed of history. Beat: horror of the ordinary; tyranny as tidiness.

chapters.title: The Palace of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Sef's POV. Sef's archivist credentials get them inside the royal archive, now a place where records are burned on a weekly schedule. Beat: Sef confronts the erasure of everything they loved.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel is brought before King Aldous. The king is polite, empty, almost kind—and for one flicker, when Mirabel's ember pendant glows, his eyes focus. Beat: the stakes made human; the man inside the ruin is still there.

chapters.title: The Regent's Offer
chapters.summary: The Regent's POV (through the crown). It offers Mirabel his mother's memories back—all of them—in exchange for the ember and his departure. Beat: temptation with a true face; it knows exactly what he wants.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel refuses—not heroically, but furiously, because his mother spent her memories to hide him, not to buy him. He escapes the throne room in a storm he can barely control. Beat: character crystallized; he chooses grief over comfort.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Archive
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef and Mirabel hide in the burning archive; Sef saves one book—her mentor's confession—and finally reads it. The betrayal was coerced; her mentor hid a fourth vault before dying. Beat: forgiveness of the dead; a new lead.

chapters.title: The Fourth Vault
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Beneath the old observatory—the one place built to watch the now-dead stars—they find the king's largest hoard of memory, warded by his mother's final co-spell. Beat: the mother's hand reaching across decades; the inheritance completes.

chapters.title: The King, Remembered
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. They begin returning the memories, but the king's mind cannot hold them: the Regent's roots are too deep. Aldous, briefly lucid, tells Mirabel there is one way—someone must anchor the returning memories with their own. Beat: the terrible price revealed.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Would Give
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He understands the anchor must be his most precious memory—the valley, his mother, the self he built. Sef begs him to find another way; there isn't one. Beat: the choice, held and turned in the light.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Night
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The moon nears completion. Mirabel spends his last free night writing himself a letter he may not be able to read, and giving Sef instructions for who he was. Beat: quiet devastation; love expressed as documentation.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the observatory, Mirabel pours his memories into Aldous as the vault opens. The Regent, starved of the king's last self, is dragged into the returning flood. Climax: storm, memory, and crown colliding.

chapters.title: The Thing Without a Crown
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The king wakes whole; the Regent, unbound from a mind with no gaps left to eat, unravels into the starless sky—and the stars, fed on released memory, begin to return. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair of Mirabel
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Mirabel survives but remembers nothing: not Sef, not the valley, not why his hands smell of rain. Sef reads him the letter he wrote himself. Beat: the cost made intimate and unbearable.

chapters.title: The King's Debt
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Restored, Aldous abolishes the memory-tithe and orders every stolen memory returned. He owes Mirabel a self he cannot repay, and knows it. Beat: justice outside the law, enacted by a king who learned what law cost.

chapters.title: A Stranger in His Own Story
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel, living in the palace as a guest of a man he doesn't remember loving, finds his mother's ember still around his neck. It's empty now—but warm. Beat: mourning without objects; grief with no address.

chapters.title: The Road Back
chapters.summary: Sef and Mirabel's POV. Sef takes Mirabel to the valley, telling him their story piece by piece on the road. At the border, the rebuilt wards recognize him anyway. Beat: the past reaching for him gently, without demand.

chapters.title: Ember, Rekindled
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the valley, holding the ember, Mirabel chooses to press it to his chest—not to restore what was lost, but to let a new memory take root where it burned. He doesn't remember his mother; he remembers that she loved him. Final beat: inheritance fulfilled—not the past returned, but the future claimed.
